overview: S3F is the outbound plugin channel, and the corpus splits by direction. The inbound machinery dominates the keyword matches: brand recognition (Grim ClientBrand, Shard ClientBrand, Truthful BrandListener, Photon BrandChannelData, intave PayloadInReader and SettingsTracker, LightAntiCheat ClientBrandRecognizer), payload frequency (Arc PayloadFrequency), payload exploits (Grim ExploitA and ExploitB), and badpackets (Frequency BadPacketsD, Hydro BadPacketsC, FlopAC BadPacketsF and BadPacketsG) all consume the client-to-server payload and appear here because the search terms overlap. The genuine S3F consumers are the anticheats' own outbound payloads: Photon rewrites the outgoing brand so clients cannot fingerprint the server, intave emits a brand-channel mark to authenticate its companion client, and Negativity sends FML handshake probes to enumerate Forge mods. Artemis and Negativity register the packet classes (SERVER_PLAY+21, CUSTOM_PAYLOAD_IN and CUSTOM_PAYLOAD_OUT).

checks.name: BrandHider (Photon)
checks.purpose: Stop clients from fingerprinting the server: rewrite every outbound brand payload to a configured fake brand.
checks.how_it_works: Two PacketAdapterBuilder listeners hook the outbound PLUGIN_MESSAGE packets (Configuration.Server and Play.Server, the S3F path) with onSendingRaw. When the channel is the brand channel (MC|Brand or minecraft:brand), the payload data is replaced with createBrandPayload of the configured brand ('Some Spigot' by default) and the packet is marked for re-encode. On join, and at an optional refresh rate, the module also pushes an empty brand payload so the adapter has something to rewrite.
checks.detects: Clients and disablers that read the server brand to pick a bypass mode; the rewrite keeps the advertised stack generic.
checks.variations: Photon's inbound twin is BrandChannelData, a ParsedPluginMessageListener that records the client brand into the user object; MessageChannel.MC_BRAND_CHANNEL is the shared channel constant.

checks.name: Sibyl brand authentication (intave)
checks.purpose: Mark the server for the Intave companion client: emit an S3F brand payload carrying the Intave identifier so the Sibyl client can authenticate.
checks.how_it_works: On join, and again on every restart broadcast and whenever a player is not yet authenticated, the service calls authentication.sendMessageToClient(player, 'MC|Brand', 'INTAVE', null), which writes the payload into an outbound custom payload packet (SibylAuthentication.java builds the ProtocolLib container around line 251). The companion client recognizes the mark and replies over its own channel.
checks.detects: Nothing cheat-related. It is the anticheat's outbound identification channel; the brand mark also lets the anticheat tell its own clients from vanilla ones.
checks.variations: The inbound side of the same system is PayloadInReader, a CUSTOM_PAYLOAD_IN reader that intave's SettingsTracker, CustomClientSupportService and LabymodClientListener consume for brand and LabyMod detection.

checks.name: FML mod probe (Negativity)
checks.purpose: Detect Forge clients by sending FML handshake payloads and reading the mod-list reply.
checks.how_it_works: initMods sends three FML|HS plugin messages (bytes {-2,0}, {0,2,0,0,0,0} and {2,0,0,0,0}) to the player when the outgoing FML channel is registered, the standard FML handshake sequence that makes Forge reply with its mod list. ChannelEvents handles the incoming FML data (the C17 side) and stores the result in the player's mod map, which feeds the mod-based cheat checks.
checks.detects: The presence and version of Forge and its mods; server owners use the result to allow or block modded clients.
checks.variations: Negativity's PacketType declares CUSTOM_PAYLOAD_IN and CUSTOM_PAYLOAD_OUT for both directions. No other anticheat probes FML; the modern anticheats read the brand channel instead.
